title: HCPCS H Codes for Behavioral Health and SUD: H0001 to H2019 Explained
summary: HCPCS H codes for behavioral health and SUD in 2026: CMS descriptors and units for H0001 to H2019 and S9480, who pays them, modifiers that change meaning by state, 15-minute and per diem unit math, H0004 vs CPT, UB-04 pairing and three state Medicaid manuals compared.
body_markdown:
HCPCS H codes are national Level II codes for mental health and substance use disorder (SUD) services, from H0001 (alcohol and/or drug assessment) to H2019 (therapeutic behavioral services) and beyond. State Medicaid programs are the main payers. Medicare pays none of them. The CMS descriptor names the service and sometimes the unit, while the state manual or payer contract decides who can bill it, how minutes become units and which modifiers go on the line.


This is a working reference for SUD and community mental health programs that bill Medicaid. It covers 2026 descriptors and units, modifiers and unit math, when payers want CPT instead, and three state manuals side by side. For the CPT side of behavioral health billing, see our[CPT codes guide](https://blog.adentris.com/cpt-codes-behavioral-health-guide/) .


The short version


- H codes are HCPCS Level II codes for mental health and SUD services. Medicaid is the main payer. Every H code, and S9480, carries coverage code I (not payable by Medicare) in CMS's October 2026 HCPCS file.
- The descriptor names the service and sometimes the unit. The state decides who may bill it, how minutes turn into units and which modifiers are required.
- Modifiers vary most. In Ohio, U1 marks a psychology assistant. In California's Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System, U1 means ASAM 3.1 residential.
- For 15-minute codes, Ohio and California use the midpoint rule, so 8 minutes earns a unit. Virginia bills whole units only.
- Program codes such as H0015, S9480, H0035 and S0201 pay one unit per day, and each payer sets its own minimum hours.
- Ohio and Virginia put licensed clinicians on CPT psychotherapy codes, not H0004, and Medicare takes only CPT. Check each payer's code table before you build charge codes.


## Why H codes exist, and who pays them


Until the end of 2003, Medicaid agencies and other payers ran their own local "Level III" codes. HIPAA's code set standards ended them. CMS's HCPCS coding procedures describe certain H codes as the ones state Medicaid agencies use when state law requires separate codes for mental health services, including alcohol and drug treatment. CMS added H0001 to H0030 in 2001 and most of the rest in 2003.


S codes come from the private side. The same CMS document says they're used primarily by private insurers and may also be used by Medicaid. Medicare doesn't pay them. Every H code in this guide, plus S9480 and S0201, carries coverage code I in CMS's file, which the 2026 record layout defines as "Not payable by Medicare." Medicare still pays for much of the same care under other codes.


Payer H codes S codes What it uses instead


**Medicare** Not payable (coverage code I) Not payable CPT codes, PHP and IOP claims with condition code 41 or 92, and weekly opioid treatment program bundles such as G2067


**Medicaid, fee-for-service and managed care** Main payer. The state manual sets the code, unit and modifiers Some states and plans. Virginia bills ASAM 2.5 with S0201 CPT for licensed clinicians in states such as Ohio


**Commercial** Plan by plan. Blue Cross NC told providers in 2021 to report H0015 for SUD IOP Blue Cross NC's notice: S9480 for mental health IOP, S0201 or H0035 for PHP Set by contract


## H codes and S9480: 2026 descriptors and units


We checked every descriptor below against CMS's October 2026 HCPCS file. They're the long form, trimmed. For H0005 through H0015 and H0020, CMS's text begins with "Alcohol and/or drug services," which we've dropped. "None stated" means the payer defines the unit.


Code CMS descriptor (long form, trimmed) Unit in descriptor


**H0001** Alcohol and/or drug assessment None stated


**H0004** Behavioral health counseling and therapy Per 15 minutes


**H0005** Group counseling by a clinician None stated


**H0006** Case management None stated


**H0010** Sub-acute detoxification (residential addiction program inpatient) None stated


**H0011** Acute detoxification (residential addiction program inpatient) None stated


**H0012** Sub-acute detoxification (residential addiction program outpatient) None stated


**H0013** Acute detoxification (residential addiction program outpatient) None stated


**H0014** Ambulatory detoxification None stated


**H0015** Intensive outpatient (treatment program that operates at least 3 hours/day and at least 3 days/week and is based on an individualized treatment plan), including assessment, counseling, crisis intervention, and activity therapies or education None stated. Paid per diem in Ohio and Virginia


**H0018** Behavioral health: short-term residential (non-hospital residential treatment program), without room and board Per diem


**H0019** Behavioral health: long-term residential (non-medical, non-acute care in a residential treatment program where stay is typically longer than 30 days), without room and board Per diem


**H0020** Methadone administration and/or service (provision of the drug by a licensed program) None stated


**H0031** Mental health assessment, by non-physician None stated


**H0032** Mental health service plan development by non-physician None stated


**H0033** Oral medication administration, direct observation None stated


**H0034** Medication training and support Per 15 minutes


**H0035** Mental health partial hospitalization, treatment, less than 24 hours None stated. Blue Cross NC pays it per diem


**H0036** Community psychiatric supportive treatment, face-to-face Per 15 minutes


**H0038** Self-help/peer services Per 15 minutes


**H0048** Alcohol and/or other drug testing: collection and handling only, specimens other than blood None stated


**H2011** Crisis intervention service Per 15 minutes


**H2012** Behavioral health day treatment Per hour


**H2014** Skills training and development Per 15 minutes


**H2015** Community support services (CMS short descriptor: "Comp comm supp svc, 15 min") Per 15 minutes


**H2016** Community support services (CMS short descriptor: "Comp comm supp svc, per diem") Per diem


**H2017** Psychosocial rehabilitation services Per 15 minutes


**H2018** Psychosocial rehabilitation services Per diem


**H2019** Therapeutic behavioral services Per 15 minutes


**H2034** Alcohol and/or drug abuse halfway house services Per diem


**H2036** Alcohol and/or other drug treatment program Per diem


**S9480** Intensive outpatient psychiatric services Per diem


**S0201** Partial hospitalization services, less than 24 hours Per diem


Watch the short descriptors. CMS's 28-character short form for every code from H0004 through H0020 reads "Alcohol and/or drug services," even for H0004 (counseling and therapy) and the behavioral health residential codes. If your billing system shows only the short form, check the long one before mapping a service.


The descriptor isn't the whole definition, either. Virginia bills ASAM 3.3 and 3.5 residential treatment with H0010, which CMS describes as sub-acute detoxification. Ohio uses H0010 for ASAM 3.2 withdrawal management, much closer to the national wording. For non-physician assessments billed as H0031 or H0001, our[90791 vs 90792 guide](https://blog.adentris.com/cpt-90791-vs-90792-psychiatric-diagnostic-evaluation/) covers the CPT alternative.


## Modifiers: HE, HF, HQ, HN to HP, TF, TG and U1 to UD


CMS publishes one descriptor per modifier. States assign their own meanings, so the same two characters can differ by state. The right column shows three current manuals.


Modifier CMS descriptor How states actually use it


**HE** Mental health program Ohio's outpatient hospital revenue code list requires HE on behavioral health lines, including revenue code 0906 (chemical dependency IOP)


**HF** Substance abuse program Ohio uses HF with H0020 for daily methadone administration at an opioid treatment program


**HQ** Group setting Ohio prices group H2019 and H0038 with HQ. California divides the group rate by 4.5, with a claim per member


**HN, HO, HP** Bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree level Ohio uses HN and HO for education level, but HP marks a trainee supervised by a physician, psychologist, CNS, CNP or PA where rates differ


**TF, TG** Intermediate level of care. Complex/high tech level of care Ohio: H0015 TG is SUD partial hospitalization and H2036 TG is ASAM 3.7. Virginia: H0010 TG is ASAM 3.3. We didn't find TF in these manuals


**U1 to UD** Medicaid level of care 1 to 13, as defined by each state California: U1 is ASAM 3.1, U8 is IOP, UB is ASAM 2.5. Ohio: U1 is a psychology assistant, U2 a licensed professional counselor, U5 an LMFT


Ohio also turns HI into ASAM 3.3 for cognitive impairment, and HG into a four-week take-home supply at an opioid treatment program. Virginia adds HB for adults and HA for adolescents on residential codes. A scrubber built on national descriptors can approve lines a state will deny, so build modifier rules from each state manual and plan billing guide.


Telehealth adds a layer. Ohio requires the GT modifier on any behavioral health service delivered by telehealth, while other payers rely on place of service 02 or 10 and modifiers such as 95, 93 or FQ. Our[telehealth billing guide for 2026](https://blog.adentris.com/telehealth-billing-behavioral-health-2026/) sorts out which payer wants what.


## How minutes become units


Nine codes in the table are billed per 15 minutes. The conversion looks trivial until three payers give three answers.


Medicare's 8-minute rule, in Chapter 5 of the Claims Processing Manual, was written for timed outpatient therapy codes: no unit under 8 minutes, one from 8 through 22, two from 23 through 37. Medicare doesn't pay H codes, so it binds no one here. States copy it, or they don't.


- **Ohio** applies the midpoint rule and prints the same chart as Medicare. A 15-minute code needs 8 minutes.
- **California's** DMC-ODS billing manual (version 4.0, July 2026) applies the midpoint rule to most codes, so a 15-minute unit is earned at 8 minutes.
- **Virginia's** ARTS manual says providers "shall not round up for partial units of service." Partial units can accumulate across a week only where span billing is allowed.


Minutes of service Ohio and California (midpoint) Virginia ARTS (whole units only)


0 to 7 0 0


8 to 14 1 0


15 to 22 1 1


23 to 29 2 1


30 to 37 2 2


38 to 44 3 2


45 to 52 3 3


53 to 59 4 3


60 to 67 4 4


A worked example: a counselor trainee delivers a 53-minute individual SUD counseling session. In Ohio that's H0004 with U7 (counselor trainee), 4 units. Under Virginia's rule it's 3 units, and the extra 8 minutes count only where span billing is allowed. A licensed clinician billing a payer that wants CPT would report one unit of 90837, which Medicare billing article A57520 assigns to 53 minutes or more.


Hourly codes have their own chart. Ohio counts one unit from 31 to 90 minutes and two from 91 to 150, and caps H2012 day treatment at 2 units a day. Units that don't match the note tend to come back as CO-16 with remark code M53, covered in our[CO-16 guide](https://blog.adentris.com/co-16-denial-code-behavioral-health/) .


## Per diem codes and the ASAM level map


Per diem codes pay one unit per date of service. Most say so in the descriptor. Two common program codes don't: H0015 describes a program of at least 3 hours a day and 3 days a week, and H0035 says only "less than 24 hours." Payers bill both per day anyway. Blue Cross NC's 2021 notice allowed one unit per date and barred PHP and IOP on the same date.


Minimum hours come from the payer, not CMS. Ohio pays the H0015 IOP per diem once group counseling passes 2 hours, and partial hospitalization (H0015 TG) once it passes 3, with no more than 12 patients per practitioner. Virginia's ARTS reimbursement structure (last updated October 2023) sets 3 hours a day for H0015 and 5 for S0201. Ohio's IOP floor sits below the H0015 descriptor's own 3 hours.


Level of care is where state coding drifts furthest. Here's one ASAM continuum in two Medicaid programs.


ASAM level Ohio Medicaid (BH manual 1.28.1, March 2026) Virginia Medicaid (DMAS ARTS service chart, 2024)


**2.1 Intensive outpatient** H0015, per diem H0015, or revenue code 0906 with H0015


**2.5 Partial hospitalization** H0015 TG, per diem S0201, or revenue code 0913 with S0201


**3.1 Low-intensity residential** H2034 H2034


**3.3 Population-specific residential** H2036 HI H0010 TG, revenue code 1002


**3.5 High-intensity residential** H2036 H0010 with HB (adult) or HA (adolescent), revenue code 1002


**3.7 Medically monitored** H2036 TG H2036 with HB or HA, revenue code 1002


**Withdrawal management and 4.0** H0012 per diem or H0014 hourly (2-WM), H0010 (3.2-WM), H0011 (3.7-WM) H0011 for ASAM 4.0, revenue code 1002


Neither state bills H0035 for SUD partial hospitalization. Its descriptor covers mental health partial hospitalization only.


## H0004 vs 90832 to 90837: when payers want CPT


H0004 and the psychotherapy codes overlap, and payers pick one on purpose. The wrong choice gets denied even when the note is perfect.


- **Medicare** takes CPT only, because H0004 isn't payable. Time thresholds for 90832, 90834 and 90837 are in our guide to[psychotherapy codes 90832, 90834 and 90837](https://blog.adentris.com/psychotherapy-cpt-codes-90832-90834-90837/) .
- **Ohio Medicaid** lists SUD H0004 only for trainees and assistants, such as counselor trainees (U7) and chemical dependency counselor assistants (U6). Licensed practitioners bill 90832 to 90838.
- **Virginia Medicaid** uses H0004 and H0005 only in opioid treatment programs and office-based addiction treatment. Elsewhere, licensed practitioners bill psychotherapy.
- **Commercial plans** set this by contract. Check the plan's behavioral health billing guide.


One rule holds everywhere: don't bill an H code and a CPT code for the same minutes. Where a payer accepts both, its manual says which provider types use which code. Your charge master should follow that line, not whichever code pays more.


## UB-04 revenue codes for IOP, PHP and residential


Facility claims on the UB-04 (837I) pair each HCPCS code with a revenue code.


- **0905** , IOP psychiatric: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan's 2023 notice uses it for mental health IOP, the service S9480 describes.
- **0906** , IOP chemical dependency: Virginia pairs it with H0015, and it's on Ohio's outpatient hospital revenue code list.
- **0912 and 0913** , partial hospitalization less intensive (half day) and intensive (full day): Virginia pairs 0913 with S0201.
- **1002** , residential treatment, chemical dependency: Virginia uses it on its ASAM 3.3 to 4.0 lines.


Medicare works differently. Hospitals and community mental health centers report condition code 41 for partial hospitalization or 92 for IOP, plus a revenue code, charge and, outside critical access hospitals, a HCPCS code for each service, such as G0410 for group psychotherapy. Hours, certification and documentation for these claims are in our[IOP and PHP billing guide](https://blog.adentris.com/iop-php-billing-documentation-guide/) .


## What to document, by code family


Reviewers check H-code claims against the descriptor and the state's service definition, so the record has to support both.


Family Codes What the record should show


**Assessment and planning** H0001, H0031, H0032 The completed assessment or plan, diagnosis, ASAM dimensions for SUD placement, credentials, date and signature. Watch caps: Ohio allows 2 H0001 assessments per patient per year per agency before prior authorization


**Timed services** H0004, H0034, H0036, H0038, H2011, H2014, H2015, H2017, H2019 Start and stop times or total minutes, who delivered it (that drives the modifier), the intervention tied to a plan goal, and the response. Virginia requires billed time to match documented time


**Program per diems** H0015, S9480, H0035, S0201, H2012 Daily attendance with times, services delivered that day, hours against the payer's minimum, level-of-care justification and an active authorization


**Residential and withdrawal management** H0010 to H0014, H0018, H0019, H2034, H2036 A fresh multidimensional reassessment at each continued-stay review, daily notes, and authorized dates that match billed days


**Medication and testing** H0020, H0033, H0048 Dose and take-home records (Ohio requires them for weekly modifiers), and collection records for H0048, which excludes lab analysis


**Group** H0005 and HQ lines Group size within the payer's cap (Ohio 12 per practitioner for IOP and PH group, Virginia 12 for H0005) and an individualized note for each member


Part 2 programs have one more check: disclosure of these records to an auditor has to fit a consent or an exception, such as the audit and evaluation rule in 42 CFR 2.53. Our[Documentation Compliance](https://adentris.com/solutions/documentation-compliance?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=hcpcs-h-codes-behavioral-health-sud&utm_content=inline) product reviews charts against Part 2 alongside Medicaid documentation rules.


## Three states, three rulebooks


The examples above come from three primary sources, checked in November 2026. Ask the same questions of any other state's manual.


Question Ohio Virginia California (DMC-ODS)


**Source** Medicaid BH manual 1.28.1, March 24, 2026 ARTS manual Chapter V, revised November 6, 2025, plus the DMAS service chart DMC-ODS billing manual 4.0, July 2026


**15-minute rounding** Midpoint, 8 minutes No rounding up, whole units Midpoint, 8 minutes


**What U modifiers mean** Practitioner type Not used on ARTS codes in the chart Level of care


**How IOP and PHP are identified** H0015 and H0015 TG H0015 and S0201 Level of care modifier U8 (IOP) or UB (ASAM 2.5) on each line


**Who bills H0004** Trainees and assistants OTP and office-based addiction treatment Named in the manual for narcotic treatment program counseling, with UA and HG


Managed care plans add their own layer of prior authorization, unit caps and modifiers. Keep a code map per payer, not per state, and date every row.


## A pre-bill checklist for H-code claims


- The payer accepts the code. Medicare doesn't.
- The code fits the payer's service definition, not just the CMS descriptor.
- The clinician is eligible for the code, and the practitioner modifier matches the credential.
- Program, level of care and group modifiers are present, in the payer's order.
- Units follow the payer's rounding rule and match documented minutes.
- Per diem days meet the payer's minimum hours, with no IOP and PHP on one date.
- The authorization covers the date, code and level of care.

## Frequently asked questions


**What are HCPCS H codes in behavioral health?**


H codes are HCPCS Level II codes for mental health and substance use services, such as alcohol and drug assessment (H0001), counseling per 15 minutes (H0004), SUD intensive outpatient (H0015) and therapeutic behavioral services (H2019). State Medicaid programs are the main payers, and each state manual sets units, modifiers and eligible practitioners.


**Does Medicare pay HCPCS H codes?**


No. Every H code carries coverage code I, "Not payable by Medicare," in CMS's October 2026 HCPCS file, and so does S9480. Medicare pays for similar care through CPT codes, PHP and IOP claims with condition code 41 or 92, and weekly G-code bundles for opioid treatment programs.


**What is the difference between H0015 and S9480?**


H0015 is alcohol and/or drug intensive outpatient treatment, which CMS describes as a program running at least 3 hours a day and 3 days a week. S9480 is intensive outpatient psychiatric services, per diem, an S code meant mainly for private payers. Blue Cross NC, for example, uses H0015 for SUD IOP and S9480 for mental health IOP, but each state or plan decides.


**How many units of H0004 do I bill for a 50-minute session?**


It depends on the payer's rounding rule. Ohio Medicaid's midpoint chart counts 38 to 52 minutes as 3 units, and Virginia's ARTS manual, which bans rounding up, also gives 3. At 53 minutes they split: 4 units in Ohio, still 3 in Virginia.


**Should I bill H0004 or a psychotherapy CPT code like 90834?**


Follow the payer. Medicare accepts only CPT. Ohio Medicaid limits SUD H0004 to trainees and assistants and has licensed practitioners bill 90832 to 90838, while Virginia limits H0004 to opioid treatment programs and office-based addiction treatment. Never bill both codes for the same minutes.


**Do U1 to UD modifiers mean the same thing in every state?**


No. CMS defines U1 to UD only as Medicaid levels of care 1 to 13, as defined by each state. California's DMC-ODS uses U1 for ASAM 3.1 residential, while Ohio uses it for a psychology assistant.
